{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-la-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c99fcb22c863e9c2b7177f5612879c1c89b83352611acd8982f1ac9fd431469b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-la-class-std:lineage:28","source_registry_sha256":"8fb2294cb50570a3a0fabb25acba3418dba999eb7dd305cc58b73fdf38975613","source_liveness_sha256":"1105a92b5841d065519de4b7fbea05111880de6d2bb8804066a972d19c63b5a0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Defensive driving, illness, fatigue and aggression","heading":"Defensive driving, illness, fatigue and aggression","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"# Defensive driving, illness, fatigue and aggression

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving behavior can be affected by personality, experience, social influences, road conditions and passengers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Defensive driving anticipates hazards instead of waiting to react after danger develops. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
A defensive driver recognizes personal limits and the limits of the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Defensive driving includes responsibility for one’s own actions and watching what others may do. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Secure passengers and pets before starting the vehicle and keep its doors locked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Driving far too slowly as well as too quickly can increase collision risk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
If drinking is planned, arrange for a designated driver who will not drink. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
Weaving, straddling the centerline, wide turns or unusual responses to signals can indicate an impaired driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
The guide suggests creating separation from a suspected impaired driver by turning off or leaving at an available exit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
Do not race another driver while merging or fight over priority. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A01
Report reckless or suspicious driving to law enforcement promptly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A02
The first SIPDE step is sweeping, searching and scanning continuously for danger. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A02
In SIPDE, identify roadway features and conditions that could become hazards. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A02
The prediction step considers how an identified hazard could conflict with the driver’s path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A02
In SIPDE, decide on a safe response and then execute the movement needed to avoid conflict. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A02
The guide names alertness, anticipation, judgment and skill as characteristics of defensive driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A02
Alert driving requires attention to surrounding details and avoiding substances that impair concentration. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A02
Anticipating hazards includes maintaining a safe gap rather than following too closely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A02
Consider hazards from pedestrians, other vehicles, weather and equipment before they require an emergency response. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A02
Sound judgment includes staying within the speed limit and slowing further for poor weather. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A02
Do not attempt to beat a train or a red signal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A02
A safe passing decision requires a safe opportunity rather than a risky maneuver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A03
Stress and strong emotions can impair driving decisions and encourage impulsive risks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A03
Predictable travel and steady lane position reduce uncertainty for other drivers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A03
Avoid driving when emotional distress makes it difficult to handle the additional demands of traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A03
Fatigue reduces attention and concentration and can slow the driver’s response. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A03
Extreme tiredness can cause brief episodes of sleep at the wheel. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A03
Begin a long trip rested and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A03
Schedule regular rest breaks and avoid travel during usual sleeping hours when possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A03
If unable to remain awake, leave the highway and stop to sleep. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0061]
